The variable OnPath is true if the motion device is on or near enough the planned program path such that program execution can continue. If the MotionDevice deviates too much from this path in case of errors or an emergency stop, this value becomes false. If OnPath is false, the motion device needs repositioning to continue program execution.
OnPath 변수는 모션 장치가 계획된 프로그램 경로에 있거나 충분히 가까워 실행을 계속할 수 있으면 TRUE이며, 오류나 비상 정지로 인해 경로에서 크게 벗어나면 FALSE가 되어 실행을 재개하려면 위치를 재조정해야 함
The variable InControl indicates whether the actuators (typically a motor) of the motion device are powered and under control; if TRUE, the device may still be in a standstill

The variable CenterOfMass provides the position and orientation of the center of mass relative to the mounting point using a 3DFrameType, where X, Y, Z define the center of gravity’s position and A, B, C define the orientation of the principal axes of inertia. For systems that do not require orientation values, A, B, and C can be set to "0".

Not all addresses (i.e. not all combinations of four integers 0-255) may be used. Many are reserved for special functions. The time setting for outputting the accumulated error amount, representing the time it takes to reach 100% output when the error is 100%. For example, if the integral time (PID I-Time) is set to 1 second, a 100% error will result in a 100% output after 1 second. The PID I-Time can be used to reduce the steady-state error.

The output amount based on the rate of change of the error. If the derivative time (PID D-Time) is set to 1 ms, and the error changes at a rate of 100% per second, 1% of the output is produced every 10 ms.

Typically, a small value (default is 0) is used to improve responsiveness, but in some cases, a larger value may be used to enhance stability. The larger the value, the more stable the PID controller output becomes, but responsiveness may decrease.
